entities.summary: Saint Nino was a 4th-century Georgian woman who played a pivotal role in the Christianization of Iberia, a region in the Caucasus that is now part of Georgia. Born around 290 AD, Nino traveled extensively throughout the region, preaching Christianity to the local nobility and eventually converting them to the faith. Her missionary work led to the establishment of the Iberian Orthodox Church and had a lasting impact on the region's history and culture. Nino's legacy extends beyond her own lifetime, with her feast day still celebrated in Georgia today. The exact circumstances of her life and death are shrouded in mystery, but her influence on the region's Christian heritage is undeniable.
